description: A sixteen-bit shift register turned into a quantised control voltage: each clock rolls the register round and now and then flips the bit coming back in, so a pattern repeats until it mutates

params.text: The chance that the bit coming back round is flipped on each clock, none fully left and every clock fully right
The chance that a gate is joined by an accent pulse, none fully left and every gate fully right; it does not change the data being injected, which is what the maker's README says it does
Pushes a set bit into the register, fires a gate and an accent at once, and works out a new voltage

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V rolls the register round by one place and works out a new voltage from it
A rising edge above 1V puts the register back to the fixed pattern it starts on
Adds to the PROB knob, 10V covering the knob's whole range, with the total held between no chance at all and every clock

outputs.text: A 1ms pulse whenever the bit newly rolled round is set, and whenever the inject button is pushed
The low eight bits of the register read as a voltage between -5V and +5V, quantised to twelfth-of-a-volt steps and held until the next clock
A 1ms pulse on the gates picked out by DENS, and on every push of the inject button

notes: nothing moves until a clock is patched to CLK IN: the shift, the gate and the voltage are all worked out on a clock edge.
the register comes up on the same fixed pattern every time, which is also what RST IN puts it back to.
the screen is drawn rather than built out of controls: the ring of sixteen dots is the register, the left arc is PROB and the right arc is DENS, and none of it can be clicked.
the maker's README describes a DATA input carrying the voltage to be sampled and shifted; no such jack exists, and the register is fed only from its own last bit.
the maker's README calls the third input an INJECT CV; the panel prints PROB CV, and adding to PROB is what it does.

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
